evidence.experimental_conditions: Formulation containing 15% sodium cocoyl isethionate; human study using a modified Draize procedure.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig modified Draize; induction: 10 intradermal injections of 0.05 ml of 0.1% pentyl salicylate in isotonic saline on alternate days; challenge: intradermal 0.05 ml of 0.1% on days 35 and 49.
evidence.support_text: Pentyl salicylate was tested in a guinea pig sensitization study using a modified Draize procedure in male and female outbred Himalayan guinea pigs weighing 400–500 g. Induction consisted of ten intradermal injections on alternate days with 0.05 ml of 0.1% pentyl salicylate in isotonic saline. Challenge on days 35 and 49 with intradermal injection of 0.05 ml of 0.1% pentyl salicylate in saline. Sensitization was not observed (Klecak et al., 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig modified Draize; induction: 4 intradermal injections of 0.1 ml of 0.05% pentyl salicylate; challenge: intradermal 0.05% and topical 10% pentyl salicylate.
evidence.support_text: Pentyl salicylate was tested in a guinea pig sensitization study using a modified Draize procedure in ten inbred Hartley albino guinea pigs with initial weight of 350 g. Induction consisted of four intradermal injections with 0.1 ml of 0.05% pentyl salicylate at 4 sites. Challenge 14 days later with intradermal injection of 0.05% pentyl salicylate (0.1 ml) and topical application of 10% pentyl salicylate (0.1 ml). A second challenge was carried out 7 days later. No sensitization reactions were observed (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig; injection challenge concentration of 0.25%; application challenge concentration of 10% (Sharp, 1978)
evidence.support_text: Benzyl alcohol was reported to be non-sensitizing at an injection challenge concentration of 0.25% and an application challenge concentration of 10% in a guinea pig modified Draize procedure (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Hartley albino guinea pigs, injection induction 0.625%, intradermal challenge 0.25%, topical challenge 30%
evidence.support_text: α-Methylbenzyl alcohol was found to be non-sensitizing in Hartley albino guinea pigs when tested in a modified Draize procedure using 0.625% as the injection induction concentration, 0.25% as the intradermal injection challenge concentration and 30% as the topical application challenge concentration (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Male and female outbred Himalayan guinea pigs (400–500 g); induction: ten intradermal injections on alternate days of 0.05 ml of 0.1% cinnamaldehyde in isotonic saline starting day 0; challenge: intradermal injection of 0.05 ml of 0.1% cinnamaldehyde in saline on days 35 and 49.
evidence.support_text: Cinnamaldehyde was tested in a guinea pig sensitization study using a modified Draize procedure. Induction consisted of ten intradermal injections on alternate days with 0.05 ml of 0.1% cinnamaldehyde in isotonic saline. Challenge on days 35 and 49 was an intradermal injection of 0.05 ml of 0.1% cinnamaldehyde. Sensitization was observed (Klecak et al., 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Hartley strain albino guinea pigs, 0.25% injection challenge, 10% application challenge, vehicle not reported
evidence.support_text: Anisyl alcohol was reported to be a non-sensitizer in Hartley strain albino guinea pigs exposed in a modified Draize procedure to 0.25% in the injection challenge and 10% in the application challenge; vehicles were not reported.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.625% benzyl formate injected intradermally at four sites on 10 Hartley albino guinea pigs; on day 14, challenged with 0.25% intradermal at one site and 20% topical at a different site; scoring 24 h later; if no reaction, induction and challenge repeated with controls. Vehicle not reported.
evidence.support_text: Benzyl formate was not sensitizing to guinea pigs in a modified Draize sensitization study. In the induction phase, a 0.625% concentration of benzyl formate was injected intradermally at four sites on 10 Hartley albino guinea pigs. On day 14, the guinea pigs were challenged with a 0.25% intradermal injection at one site and 20% topical concentration at a different site. Scoring was done 24 h later. In the absence of a sensitization reaction in the first challenge the induction and challenge procedures were repeated, but this time a confirmatory challenge with controls was included irrespective of any apparent sensitization reaction at the previous challenge. The vehicle was not reported (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10 albino Hartley guinea pigs; induction: 0.1% 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone intradermally at four sites; challenge on day 14: 0.1% intradermal at one site and 5% topical at a different site; scoring 24 h later.
evidence.support_text: In a modified Draize sensitization test with 10 albino Hartley guinea pigs, 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone was sensitizing after two sensitization treatments using 0.1% intradermal induction and challenge with 0.1% intradermal and 5% topical.

evidence.support_text: Methyl cinnamate was tested in a Modified Draize test at 0.1% in saline on male and female outbred Himalayan guinea pigs, and sensitization effects were observed (Klecak et al., 1977).

evidence.support_text: Sensitization potential of nerolidol was measured in a guinea pig (10 male and female inbred Hartley strain albino guinea pigs/group) using a modified Draize procedure. The animals were induced intradermally with 1% and challenged with 1% (ICC) and 20% (ACC). A second challenge was carried out 7 days later. Reactions were examined under a Philips color-matching unit. No sensitization was observed (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, induction 0.25%, challenge 0.1% and 5%
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig modified Draize test, hexyl salicylate induced sensitization at induction concentration 0.25% and challenge concentrations 0.1% and 5% (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.1 ml of hexyl salicylate at 0.1% (ICC) intradermally at four sites; challenge: 0.1 ml of 0.1% intradermally and 5% topically; species: Hartley albino guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a modified Draize test, Hartley albino guinea pigs with initial weights of approximately 350 g each. Induction consisted of four intradermal injections with 0.1 ml of hexyl salicylate at 2.5 times the ICC (Injection Challenge Concentration = 0.1%) at four sites overlying the two auxillary and the two inguinal lymph nodes. The animals were challenged 14 days later with an intradermal injection in one flank and a topical application in the other flank using 0.1 ml hexyl salicylate at 0.1% (ICC) and 5% (ACC), respectively. A second challenge was conducted 7 days later. Sensitization reactions were observed after the second challenge (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intradermal induction: 0.1% (vehicle not specified); Intradermal challenge: 0.1% (vehicle not specified); Topical challenge: 5% (vehicle not specified); Hartley albino guinea pigs (4 or 6 of each sex, 10 total); reference Sharp (1978)
evidence.support_text: Hexyl salicylate was tested in the modified Draize test. Intradermal induction at 0.1% and challenge at 0.1% (intradermal) and 5% (topical) resulted in sensitization in Hartley albino guinea pigs (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.support_text: In a modified Draize test with induction at 0.1% intradermal and challenge at 0.1% intradermal and 5% topical (2 challenge doses), 2-hexylidene cyclopentanone was classified as sensitizing in guinea pigs.

evidence.support_text: A modified Draize procedure in 10 Hartley guinea pigs with 0.25% cinnamyl alcohol induction and 0.1% and 10% challenge. No sensitization reactions were observed (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.support_text: A modified Draize procedure in Himalayan guinea pigs using 0.1% cinnamyl alcohol in saline for induction and challenge. Sensitization was not observed (Klecak et al., 1977).

evidence.support_text: In the Human Repeat Insult Patch Test, PPD at an induction dose of 1% (1000 µg/cm²) gave 47/88 positive reactions (53.4%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Moisturizing lotion containing 0.25% myristyl alcohol, occlusive patches, 10 induction applications, 229 participants
evidence.support_text: A moisturizing lotion containing 0.25% myristyl alcohol was applied to the backs of 229 male and female participants via occlusive patches for 24 hours with 10 induction applications; none of the participants had reactions to the product.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Pump spray antiperspirant containing 5.0% isostearyl alcohol, 148 participants, reactions suggestive of sensitization, followed by rechallenge with product
evidence.support_text: A pump spray antiperspirant containing 5.0% isostearyl alcohol evaluated in 148 participants resulted in 10 participants with reactions suggestive of sensitization; on rechallenge with the product 2 months later, 6 participants had reactions, confirming sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: reported in Natsch et al., 2012
evidence.support_text: Benzaldehyde induced sensitization in a Human Repeat Insult Patch Test (Natsch et al., 2012).

evidence.support_text: In 2 separate confirmatory human repeat insult patch tests with 1938 µg/cm² of the read-across material 2-(4-methylphenoxy)ethanol, no reactions indicative of sensitization was observed in any of the 10 and 34 volunteers (RIFM, 1971; RIFM, 1972).

evidence.support_text: In the human repeat insult patch test with up to 8% (9448 µg/cm²) benzyl acetate in ethanol:diethylphthalate (75:25), no reactions indicative of skin sensitization were observed (RIFM, 1987; RIFM, 1988a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: liquid/powder foundation containing benzoic acid 0.2%, n=75
evidence.support_text: In a clinical study, a liquid/powder foundation containing benzoic acid (0.2%) produced no reactions at induction or challenge (n=75).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% (1550 µg/cm2) butanoic acid, 3a,4,5,6,7,7a-hexahydro-4,7-methano-1H-indenyl ester; 112 human subjects
evidence.support_text: In a human confirmatory repeat insult patch test (HRIPT), no reactions indicative of sensitization were observed in 112 subjects with 5% (1550 µg/cm2) butanoic acid, 3a,4,5,6,7,7a-hexahydro-4,7-methano-1H-indenyl ester (RIFM, 2001a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Healthy volunteers; EPI-10 patch applied for 12 h during induction and challenge; skin scores graded 0-2; 28 subjects enrolled.
evidence.support_text: EPI-10 was locally perfectly tolerated by more than 70% of subjects, provoking only very mild or mild transient erythema that disappeared spontaneously 1–5 h after patch removal, and did not provoke skin reactions due to sensitization. The challenge patch did not provoke any skin reaction besides the transient erythema, and the incidence and severity of erythema after challenge were not increased compared to induction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: nine consecutive applications over 3 weeks, 2-week rest period, then a challenge application; skin reactions evaluated over 72 h
evidence.support_text: A skin sensitization study evaluated the effects of repeated application of OTG in 201 subjects. After nine consecutive applications over 3 weeks and a 2-week rest period, a challenge application was applied and skin reactions were evaluated over 72 h. 93% of subjects receiving OTG were free of any skin reaction, and a single subject (0.5%) experienced a mild sensitization response characterized by mild erythema with papules.

evidence.assay_type: human repeat insult patch test (Jordan-King modification of Draize procedure)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Occlusive patch application; induction phase on upper outer arms with continuous contact; challenge phase on mid to upper back with 48 hr occluded application; scoring at 30 min, 24, 48, 72 hr after patch removal; 250 subjects enrolled, 242 completed irritation phase, 237 completed challenge phase; negative control distilled water, positive control sodium lauryl sulfate 0.05%
evidence.support_text: In a single-blind, randomized, assessor-blind, controlled study of naftifine 2% cream (NAFT-2) using the Jordan-King modification of the Draize procedure with induction and challenge phases in 250 healthy volunteers, NAFT-2 showed one potential sensitization response in the challenge phase that did not repeat on rechallenge. The authors concluded that NAFT-2 would not be considered a primary sensitizer and would likely demonstrate a maximal population rate of 1.5% likelihood for observing sensitization in clinical use.

evidence.assay_type: human repeat insult patch test (maximization test)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: SLS pretreatment (5% aqueous, 1 h), then eye shadow applied under occlusion for 48-72 h, repeated for 5 exposures; Challenge: 5% SLS pretreatment 1 h, then single application of eye shadow under occlusion for 48 h; 25 subjects completed.
evidence.support_text: In a human repeat insult patch test (maximization design), an eye shadow containing 1.5% Glyceryl Dilaurate was applied to 25 subjects after SLS pretreatment on the same site. Induction: SLS pretreatment (5% aqueous, 1 h) followed by occlusive application of the eye shadow for 48-72 h, repeated for 5 exposures. After a 10-day rest, challenge: 1 h SLS pretreatment then a single application of the eye shadow under occlusion for 48 h at a new site. Neither contact allergy nor any adverse reaction was observed in any of the 25 subjects who completed the study. It was concluded that the eye shadow containing 1.5% Glyceryl Dilaurate does not possess a detectable contact-sensitizing potential (Ivy Laboratories 1997).

evidence.assay_type: human repeat insult patch test (maximization test)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Procedure identical to preceding maximization test for the eye shadow; 27 subjects completed.
evidence.support_text: Ivy Laboratories (1999) evaluated the skin sensitization potential of a foundation containing 1.5% Glyceryl Dilaurate using the same maximization test procedure. Twenty-seven subjects completed the study; one was lost to follow-up. Neither contact allergy nor any other adverse reaction was observed in any of the 27 subjects. It was concluded that the foundation containing 1.5% Glyceryl Dilaurate does not possess a detectable contact-sensitizing potential.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Volunteer testing at sufficiently high levels; exact protocol not specified.

evidence.experimental_conditions: repeated weekly patch-test applications; concentration not specified

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% Ascorbic Acid in test sample; induction phase with 0.25% aqueous SLS pretreatment followed by 48 h test material application, repeated for 5 exposures; challenge phase with 5% aqueous SLS pretreatment for 1 h, then 48 h occlusion; grading at 1 h and 24 h after removal.
evidence.support_text: Under the conditions of this test, the test sample with 10% Ascorbic Acid did not possess a detectable contact-sensitizing potential and hence is not likely to cause contact sensitivity under normal use conditions (KGL, Inc. 1998). The induction protocol used a 24-h SLS pretreatment followed by 48 h of test material application for a total of 5 induction exposures, and after a 10-day rest period a challenge patch was applied with SLS pretreatment for 1 hour.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% Nonoxynol-2 in mineral oil, human repeat-insult patch test
evidence.support_text: In a human repeat-insult patch test, 10% Nonoxynol-2 in mineral oil induced allergic contact dermatitis in 9 of 103 subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% Nonoxynol-2 in mineral oil, human repeat-insult patch test
evidence.support_text: In a human repeat-insult patch test, 5% Nonoxynol-2 in mineral oil showed no evidence of allergic contact dermatitis in any of the 102 subjects tested.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 7.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide; induction phase with 9 applications over 3 weeks; challenge after 2-week non-treatment; readings at 48 h and 96 h
evidence.support_text: In a human repeat-insult patch test with 7.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide, 1+ reactions (erythema throughout the entire patch area) were observed in 53 subjects and 2+ reactions (erythema and edema) in three subjects during induction; these were considered mild irritation. Two subjects had 1+ reactions at 48- and 96-h challenge readings. The researchers concluded 'no evidence of sensitization' to 7.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide (International Research Services, Inc. 1997).

evidence.experimental_conditions: repeat-insult patch test; 50% w/v Glyceryl Palmitate Lactate in subjects; human
evidence.support_text: Glyceryl Palmitate Lactate (50% w/v) did not induce skin irritation or sensitization in subjects patch tested in a repeat-insult patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Test material: facial wash (1% raw material containing 35% to 36.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide); 0.2 ml on semi-occlusive Webril/adhesive patch; 9 induction patches (24 h application, 24 h nonapplication, 48 h on weekends); challenge after 2-week non-treatment; readings at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h
evidence.support_text: In a repeat-insult patch test using a facial wash (1% raw material containing 35% to 36.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide), 189 subjects completed. No significant reactions were noted during induction or challenge; only one ± reaction at 48-h post-challenge. It was concluded that Cocamidopropylamine Oxide did not induce dermal sensitization (Harrison Research Laboratories, Inc. 2001a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: repeat-insult patch test; test material was a facial wash containing 1% raw material (the raw material contained 35% to 36.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide); 252 subjects empaneled (age 18–65), 199 completed; induction phase: 3 subjects scored ± (faint minimal erythema); challenge phase: 24 subjects scored ± and 6 subjects scored 1 (erythema); conclusion: test material did not induce contact dermal sensitization
evidence.support_text: Harrison Research Laboratories, Inc. (1993) performed a repeat-insult patch test study using a facial wash containing 1% raw material (which itself contained 35% to 36.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide). Out of 252 subjects, 199 completed. During induction, 3 subjects scored ± (faint, minimal erythema). During the challenge phase, 24 subjects scored ± and 6 subjects scored a 1 (erythema). It was concluded that the test material did not induce contact dermal sensitization in human subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Tested in approximately 2175 volunteers; concentration and vehicle not specified in passage.
evidence.support_text: In induction of dermal sensitization measured by standard human repeat-insult patch tests and maximization tests in approximately 2175 volunteers, 1,1-dimethylphenethyl formate showed a sensitization reaction in 1 of 24 study participants. However, all such reactions were likely related to adjacent testing of a known dermal sensitizer, and the compound exhibited a lack of sensitization in comparative tests; thus the result is considered equivocal.

Glyceryl Laurate induced mild, erythematous reactions during induction in most of the subjects and questionable reactions during the challenge phase in seven subjects. During induction and challenge phases, reactions to Glyceryl Laurate ranged from 1 (mild erythema) to 2 (moderate erythema).
Glyceryl Linoleate did not induce skin irritation or sensitization in a human repeat-insult patch test with 74 subjects completing the study (16 withdrawals unrelated to treatment, 1 due to pain).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Controlled study; 133 subjects; MTS applied to same skin site for 3 weeks.
evidence.support_text: In a controlled study designed to explore skin sensitization, 18 of 133 subjects (13.5%) were confirmed to have become sensitized after intentionally applying MTS (methylphenidate transdermal system) to the same skin site for 3 weeks.

evidence.assay_type: human repeated insult occlusive patch test
evidence.experimental_conditions: repeated insult, occlusive patch test; 50% w/w Glyceryl Dioleate in subjects; human
evidence.support_text: Sensitization was not induced in subjects patch tested with 50% w/w Glyceryl Dioleate in a repeated insult, occlusive patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.2 mL undiluted; occluded; 9 applications over 3 weeks; challenge on virgin site 2 weeks after last induction; scoring at removal and 72/96 h; 208 volunteers
evidence.support_text: In a human repeated insult patch test, undiluted di-n-butyl terephthalate (0.2 mL) was applied under occlusion to the upper backs of 208 volunteers for nine applications over three weeks, with challenge patches applied two weeks after the last induction. Di-n-butyl terephthalate showed no potential for dermal sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.25% 1,1-diethoxyhexane
evidence.support_text: In a human repeated insult patch test, no skin sensitization reactions were observed with 0.25% 1,1-diethoxyhexane (RIFM, 1965).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.25% 1,1-diethoxyhexane administered to human subjects in a repeated insult patch test (RIFM, 1965)
evidence.support_text: No predictive skin sensitization studies are available for 1,1-diethoxyhexane. However, in a human repeated insult patch test, no skin sensitization reactions were observed with 0.25% 1,1-diethoxyhexane (RIFM, 1965).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% DEHT in acetone induction; 203 volunteers; 3 times/week for 3 weeks; semi-occluded; challenge with 2% DEHT in acetone; scoring 48 and 96 h after challenge
evidence.support_text: DEHT as a 0.5% solution in acetone was applied to the back of 203 human volunteers three times per week for three weeks using semi-occluded patches, with challenge patches of 2% DEHT in acetone applied to naïve sites two weeks later. Only two subjects showed minimal erythema (slight, confluent or patchy), and the authors concluded there was no evidence that DEHT caused dermal sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1.25% 2-heptylcyclopentanone in ethanol (969 µg/cm²); 0.5 ml on 1×1 inch Webril swatch, occlusive patch applied to upper arm for 24 h; induction phase: 9 applications over 3 weeks (Mon/Wed/Fri); after 10–14 day rest, challenge patch on previously unexposed site; reactions scored at 24, 48, and 72 h after challenge.
evidence.support_text: A repeated insult patch test was conducted to determine if 1.25% 2-heptylcyclopentanone in ethanol (969 µg/cm²) would induce dermal sensitization in human volunteers. During the induction phase, 0.5 ml was applied to a Webril swatch under occlusive conditions to the upper arm for 24 h on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday for 9 applications over 3 weeks. After a 10- to 14-day rest period, a challenge patch was applied to a new site, scored at 24, 48, and 72 h. There was no reaction in 40 volunteers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1.5% PEG-6 Stearate in hair cream, 4 occlusive patches per week for 2 weeks, challenge after 2 weeks
evidence.support_text: CTFA reported that a 1.5% PEG-6 Stearate hair cream tested for potential skin sensitization produced all challenge scores of zero, indicating no allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10 test applications over a 24-day period with a single challenge 14 to 21 days later; 52 human subjects
evidence.support_text: A repeated insult patch test was conducted using 52 humans in which 10 test applications of TRIS were made over a 24-day period with a single challenge 14 to 21 days later. TRIS did not elicit any skin sensitization or any other dermal reactions in any of the subjects tested [28].

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10-day dermal exposure followed 14 days later by a challenge exposure; triclosan administered at 1%, 5%, or 20% in an unspecified vehicle; study in human adult volunteers
evidence.support_text: In a sensitization study by Marzulli and Maibach (1973), triclosan was administered to human volunteers at concentrations of 1%, 5%, or 20% using standard sensitization testing methods with a 10-day dermal exposure followed by a challenge 14 days later. No evidence of sensitization was reported.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 100% test material, human
evidence.support_text: Similarly, no sensitization reactions were reported in a human repeated insult patch test conducted with 100% α-methylcyclohexylmethyl acetate (RIFM, 1977a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tests performed with leaves, stems, and bark of Hedera helix (common ivy). Tested on a 52-year-old male mechanic. 10 control subjects tested negative.
evidence.support_text: A 52-year-old male mechanic presented with dermatitis and marked swelling of the face after pruning common ivy (Hedera helix) and poison ivy. Patch tests with the leaves, stems, and bark of common ivy were positive; 10 controls were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patients were treated therapeutically for warts with 20% resorcinol; subsequent patch testing.
evidence.support_text: When the skin of 24 patients was treated with 20% resorcinol for warts, subsequent patch testing showed that 23 out of 24 patients reacted positively to resorcinol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: poultice application; 1 day use
evidence.support_text: Our case showed allergic contact dermatitis from flurbiprofen in a poultice after 1-day use.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Product tested 'as is'; readings at 48 and 72 hours; patient with diffuse eczematous rash.
evidence.support_text: Patch tests to the European standard and cosmetic series were all negative. Contact allergy to the patient's cream was suspected and confirmed by patch testing to the product 'as is': there were ++ at 48 h and 72 h.

evidence.experimental_conditions: PTBC concentration up to 0.5%; patch applied on human skin; reported in Horio et al., 1977
evidence.support_text: A literature report cited in the study indicates that a PTBC concentration of up to 0.5% induced contact sensitivity when patch tested on human skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: PTBFR at 10% in petrolatum (as per standard patch testing)
evidence.support_text: Shoe dermatitis (A) in a patient with positive patch test reactions to PTBFR, potassium dichromate, and shoe pieces (B).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Semiocclusive patch containing SLS Castor Wax extract (concentration not stated) applied for 24 and 48 hours; reactions scored at 24 and 48 hours post-removal; three patients with occupational hypersensitivity to castor allergens.
evidence.support_text: Lehrer et al. (1980) reported that three patients hypersensitive to castor allergen had a positive patch test reaction to the SLS Castor Wax extract.

evidence.experimental_conditions: SLS Castor Wax extract tested at up to 22,000 µg/ml; other three extracts concentrations not stated; patch test on 7 normal subjects and 3 patients with occupational hypersensitivity to castor allergens.
evidence.support_text: None of the seven subjects (normal) and none of the three patients with occupational hypersensitivity to castor allergens patch tested with the SLS Castor Wax extract (up to 22,000 µg/ml) or the remaining three extracts of Castor Wax (concentrations not stated) had a delayed skin reaction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: St John's Institute of Dermatology, London, 1991-2006; age group ≤40 years
evidence.support_text: Among patients aged ≤40 years patch tested with methyldibromo glutaronitrile, 86 out of 9850 (0.86%) had a positive reaction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: St John's Institute of Dermatology, London, 1991-2006; baseline series containing methyldibromo glutaronitrile; age groups ≤40 and >40 years
evidence.support_text: In a study of 17776 patients patch tested with a baseline series including methyldibromo glutaronitrile at St John's Institute of Dermatology from 1991 to 2006, the overall prevalence of positive patch tests was 235/18011 (1.31%). A highly significant association with age >40 years was found (p<0.0001).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Standard patch test allergens (Trolab); concentration not specified; reading at day 2 and day 3 typical
evidence.support_text: 4 of 5 hospital employees with hand dermatitis showed positive patch test reaction to 1,3-diphenylguanidine (DPG); all had been using gloves containing this rubber additive.

evidence.experimental_conditions: standard patch test methodology (concentration not specified)
evidence.support_text: In a summary of 58 cases of contact dermatitis following henna tattoos, 42 patients had patch testing documented: 83% (35) were positive to para-phenylenediamine (PPD).

evidence.experimental_conditions: standard patch test, read after 48 h; aqueous solution at unspecified concentration
evidence.support_text: Table 1 shows that 9 patients had positive patch test reactions (+), and 2 had equivocal reactions (±), to an aqueous solution of Phenergan (promethazine) when tested on 83 patients suspected of intolerance. The paper notes the relatively small number of reactions to the solution compared to the cream.

evidence.experimental_conditions: standard patch test, read after 48 h; concentration not specified
evidence.support_text: Table 1 from patch tests on 83 patients shows that 45 had positive reactions (+), and 2 had equivocal reactions (±), to Phenergan cream. The paper notes the cream vehicle itself produced reactions in 40 of 83 patients, raising the possibility of irritation or combined effects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: standard series (GEIDC) and oil series
evidence.support_text: In 230 patients with occupational dermatitis in the metallurgic industry, responses to benzisothiazolone in standard patch tests (GEIDC and an oil series) were among the main positive results.

evidence.experimental_conditions: standard series (GEIDC) and oil series
evidence.support_text: In 230 patients with occupational dermatitis in the metallurgic industry, responses to Grotan BK® in standard patch tests (GEIDC and an oil series) were among the main positive results.

evidence.experimental_conditions: standard series (GEIDC) and oil series
evidence.support_text: In 230 patients with occupational dermatitis in the metallurgic industry, responses to triethanolamine in standard patch tests (GEIDC and an oil series) were among the main positive results.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Test concentration: 1% in water; years: 1981–1983; number of patients: 230; occlusion: not stated.
evidence.support_text: A Spanish study from 1981–1983 tested 230 metalworkers with possible occupational dermatitis using 1% tris(N-hydroxyethyl)hexahydrotriazine in water and found 7.0% positive reactions (reference 23).

evidence.support_text: An Israeli study from 1999–2003 tested 175 patients with suspected occupational contact dermatitis working with oil and cooling fluids; 1% tris(N-hydroxyethyl)hexahydrotriazine in water gave 1.7% positive reactions (reference 16).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Test concentration: 1% in water; years: 2001–2007; number of patients tested: 1166; number of positive reactions: 24; occlusion: not stated.
evidence.support_text: At the Finnish Institute of Occupational Health, among 1166 patients suspected of occupational contact dermatitis tested between 2001 and 2007, there were 24 positive patch test reactions to 1% tris(N-hydroxyethyl)hexahydrotriazine in water (reference 32). evidence.experimental_conditions: Test concentration: 1% in water; years: 2004–2005; number of patients: 37; occlusion: not stated.
evidence.support_text: In the same IVDK study (2004–2005) with 37 patients with suspected metalworking fluid dermatitis, patch testing with 1% tris(N-hydroxyethyl)hexahydrotriazine in water gave 8.1% positive reactions (reference 14).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Test concentration: 5%

evidence.experimental_conditions: tested at 2%; total dermatitis patients (population not specified)

evidence.experimental_conditions: tested at 2%; total dermatitis patients (population not specified)

evidence.experimental_conditions: tested at 5–20%
evidence.support_text: When tested at 5–20%, no skin reaction was observed [186]. It is very minimally skin reactive [8].

evidence.experimental_conditions: Tested with 0.01% glyceryl monoisostearate via occlusive patch; patient had history of facial erythema from foundation containing 1.77% glyceryl diisostearate.
evidence.support_text: A 35-year-old female patient with itchy, facial erythema resulting from a foundation containing 1.77% glyceryl diisostearate gave a strong positive reaction when patch tested with 0.01% glyceryl monoisostearate. Glyceryl monoisostearate was an impurity detected in glyceryl diisostearate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application of 0.1% cream formulation in clinical trial
evidence.support_text: In a limited clinical trial of a stable cream formulation containing 0.1% of Compound 15, skin reactions appeared in 6% of patients. Positive patch tests to this thiocyanate were obtained in several of them, indicating that Compound 15 can cause sensitisation in man.

evidence.experimental_conditions: undiluted under occlusion
evidence.support_text: In a patch test study with undiluted 1-(3-methyl-2-benzofuranyl)ethenone under occlusion, no skin reactions were observed in 48 subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Unknown patch test concentration and vehicle; patients from North American Contact Dermatitis Group study in 2002.
evidence.support_text: When investigated by the North American Contact Dermatitis Group in 2002, the results were unexpectedly high with 0.7% of patch test patients having a positive reaction to lidocaine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Various concentrations and vehicles; numerous studies on diverse patient groups (see supporting references)
evidence.support_text: No effects due to patch-testing with DEP were found in a series of studies: in a 58-year-old woman with contact dermatitis from eyeglass nose pads (Jordan and Dahl, 1971), in a 62-year-old woman with perfume-associated dermatitis (Larsen, 1975), in 38 contact dermatitis patients (Ishihara, 1977), in nine children with dry plantar dermatosis (Schulsinger and Mollgaard, 1980), in a patient with psoriasis (de Groot and Liem, 1983), in a patient with itchy dermatitis after perfumed lotion (van Ketel, 1983), in 21 patients allergic to perfumes (Meynadier et al., 1986), in a 35-year-old teacher with dermatitis (de Leeuw and den Hollander, 1987), in a 73-year-old woman with itchy pigmentation (Hayakawa et al., 1987), in 70 dermatitis patients (Nethercott et al., 1989), in two chronic hand eczema patients (Farli et al., 1990), in 115 cosmetic-related contact allergy patients (Remaut, 1992), in a patient with tea tree oil sensitivity (de Groot and Weyland, 1992), in 82 occupational acrylic sensitization patients (Guerra et al., 1993), and in 51 variety allergy patients (Holness and Nethercott, 1997).

evidence.experimental_conditions: vehicle not specified; reading at 72 hours
evidence.support_text: A case of erythema multiforme–like dermatitis was diagnosed with acral involvement, a positive patch test to isoniazid (INH), and lymphocytic inflammation in a skin biopsy. evidence.experimental_conditions: Visotrast 290, as is, patch test on skin after stripping, readings at 24 h, 48 h, 72 h
evidence.support_text: In the retest (Table 2) after skin stripping, Case 1 showed a positive reaction to Visotrast 290 (as is) with ++* at 48 h.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Visotrast 370, as is, patch test on skin after stripping, readings at 24 h, 48 h, 72 h

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with Inimur® Vaginalstäbchen on a 40-year-old female patient; performed during symptom-free interval.
evidence.support_text: A 40-year-old female patient developed erosive hemorrhagic contact eczema on the vagina and vulva after treatment with Inimur® Vaginalstäbchen. Type IV sensitization against Inimur® Vaginalstäbchen was confirmed by epicutaneous patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 21-day induction phase (three consecutive 7-day applications) followed by a 7-day challenge phase in healthy subjects; granisetron transdermal patch
evidence.support_text: In a phase I randomized double-blind study, a granisetron transdermal patch was tested for skin sensitization. During the challenge phase, 1 out of 200 subjects (0.5%) had a positive sensitization reaction, classified by the investigator as erythema with vesicles, delayed marked pruritus, and extension of skin reaction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test according to International Contact Dermatitis Research Group (ICDRG) recommendations; patients with eczematous cheilitis; study conducted in Singapore, 1996-1999.
evidence.support_text: In a retrospective study by Lim and Goh (2000), 202 consecutive patients with eczematous cheilitis were patch-tested according to ICDRG recommendations. Twenty-nine patients (2 males, 27 females) had positive reactions to Ricinoleic Acid. Of the 29 reactions, 22 were considered relevant positives.

evidence.experimental_conditions: elastopatches to inner arm; 48 h removal; retest after 2 weeks; same procedure
evidence.support_text: A group of 223 subjects (18-34 years, normal skin) was patch tested with 0.55N Ammonium Thioglycolate (≥6.0% solution, pH 9.3). Reactions were observed in 24 subjects. Of 213 subjects retested 2 weeks later, 26 had an immediate reaction, and 1 of these had a delayed reaction. The authors concluded that 0.55N Ammonium Thioglycolate induced skin irritation and sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patches (same lotion) applied, retest of 15 subjects
evidence.support_text: A separate group of 863 subjects (140 with diseased skin, 723 normal) was patch tested with the same hair waving lotion. Reactions (type not specified) were observed in 16 subjects. When 15 of the subjects were retested, 2 had definitely positive reactions. Prior to testing, these 2 subjects had had 5 and 3 cold waves, respectively.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patches remained for 48 h to 7 days; retest after 20-40 days
evidence.support_text: A hair waving lotion (pH 9.21, containing 4.61% Thioglycolic Acid and 0.86% ammonia) was patch tested on 286 patients with various skin conditions. Skin irritation was not observed in any patient. When patch tests were repeated (109 patients) 20 to 40 days later, sensitization reactions were not observed.

evidence.assay_type: human patch test (retest with modified procedure)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Nonoxynol-2 10% in mineral oil; semiocclusive patch applied for 30 min, then rinsed with warm water; reactions scored at 24 h post application (seven subjects) and also at 48 h for one subject.
evidence.support_text: Seven of the nine subjects with contact allergic dermatitis from the initial test were retested with a different procedure: the test substance (Nonoxynol-2 10% in mineral oil) was applied under a semiocclusive patch for 30 min, then rinsed with warm water. Reactions were scored at 24 h post application (seven subjects) and at 24 and 48 h post application (one subject). In the retest, mild allergic responses were observed in two of seven subjects; reactions were not observed in the remaining five.

evidence.experimental_conditions: topical application of sulfonamide ointment to an artificial burn on volunteers (n=259)
evidence.support_text: Sulzberger's demonstration that he could sensitize the skin of 19 per cent of 259 volunteers with sulfonamide ointment is impressive. An artificial burn was the site of application.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 21-day induction phase with three consecutive granisetron patch applications every 7 days, followed by a challenge phase with patch application to an alternative skin site; irritation scored 0-4.
evidence.support_text: During the challenge phase of a phase I, randomized, double-blind study evaluating the granisetron transdermal delivery system (patch), one out of 200 subjects (0.5%) had a positive sensitization reaction, classified by the investigator as erythema with vesicles, delayed marked pruritus, and extension of skin reaction. The study involved a 21-day induction phase with three consecutive patch applications every 7 days followed by a challenge phase at an alternative skin site.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with castor oil (as is) according to ICDRG basic standards using Finn chambers and Scanpor tape; 103 patients suspected of having cosmetic-related contact dermatitis (ages not stated).
evidence.support_text: In a study by Hashimoto et al. (1990), 103 patients suspected of having cosmetic-related contact dermatitis were patch tested with castor oil (as is) according to ICDRG basic standards. One patient had a positive patch test reaction to castor oil. No positive photopatch test reactions were reported.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% Coal Tar
evidence.support_text: A psoriasis patient had positive allergic reactions to a patch test with Coal Tar diluted to 1% (Clark and Sheretz 1998).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% ethylenediamine dihydrochloride in methylcellulose vehicle, observation within 15 minutes
evidence.support_text: Patch testing was performed using 1% ethylenediamine dihydrochloride in a methylcellulose vehicle. Within 15 min, the patient developed a 1-cm papule at the test site, surrounded by diffuse erythema of the volar forearm, diffuse pruritus, erythema over the palms and face, and eye irritation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% in unspecified vehicle, tested in dermatitis patients (313 subjects)
evidence.support_text: In a diagnostic patch test study by Frosch et al. (1995), OTNE at 1% concentration produced a positive reaction in 1 out of 313 dermatitis patients (frequency 0.3%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: THP-1 human monocytic cell line; concentration and exposure time not specified in the passage.
evidence.support_text: DBP alone failed to induce the release of IL-8 from THP-1 cells.

evidence.experimental_conditions: THP-1 human monocytic cell line; concentration and exposure time not specified in the passage.
evidence.support_text: The exposure of THP-1 cells to Cit and IMZ revealed a statistically significant release of IL-8 compared to vehicle treated cells.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application on reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) in 3D coculture with human dendritic cells; 0.2% limonene-OOHs (20 µg/cm²).
evidence.support_text: Using a 3D coculture model with reconstructed human epidermis and dendritic cells, no DC activation was detected after topical application of 0.2% limonene-OOHs (20 µg/cm²).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application on reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) in 3D coculture with human dendritic cells; 1.2% limonene-1-OOH.
evidence.support_text: Using a 3D coculture model with reconstructed human epidermis and dendritic cells, topical application of 1.2% limonene-1-OOH induced DC activation. Limonene-1-OOH was stronger than limonene-2-OOH with respect to both frequency and magnitude of responses.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application on reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) in 3D coculture with human dendritic cells; 2% limonene-2-OOH.
evidence.support_text: Using a 3D coculture model with reconstructed human epidermis and dendritic cells, topical application of 2% limonene-2-OOH induced DC activation.

evidence.assay_type: CD1a immunohistochemistry with DAB-stained pixel distribution analysis
evidence.experimental_conditions: Ex vivo human skin samples; exposure to 30 ppm MCI in H2O vehicle; 4 independent experiments (Exp4–7) with 3–5 sections each; time not specified.
evidence.support_text: When skin was exposed to 30 ppm methylchloroisothiazolinone (MCI), no statistical difference in DAB-stained pixel distribution was observed in 3 out of 4 experiments compared to the H2O vehicle, indicating that the dose was not sufficient to induce Langerhans cell migration across the epidermis.

evidence.assay_type: CD1a immunohistochemistry with DAB-stained pixel distribution analysis
evidence.experimental_conditions: Ex vivo human skin samples; exposure to 30 ppm MI in H2O vehicle; 4 independent experiments (Exp4–7) with 3–5 sections each; time not specified.
evidence.support_text: In four independent experiments with human skin, exposure to 30 ppm methylisothiazolinone (MI) caused a significant statistical difference in the DAB-stained pixel distribution across the epidermis compared to the vehicle (H2O) control, indicating that MI induced Langerhans cell migration through the epidermis, consistent with a skin sensitization reaction.

evidence.assay_type: CD1a immunohistochemistry with DAB-stained pixel distribution analysis
evidence.experimental_conditions: Ex vivo human skin samples; exposure to 600 ppm MI in H2O vehicle; 4 independent experiments; time not specified.
evidence.support_text: At 600 ppm methylisothiazolinone (MI), the DAB-stained pixel distribution differed significantly from the H2O vehicle control in 2 out of 4 tested skin samples. The visual analysis of CD1a immunohistology slides suggested a higher number of Langerhans cells in the dermis compared to the epidermis, supporting that at 600 ppm MI likely acts more as a skin irritant than a skin sensitizer.

evidence.assay_type: CD86 expression on Langerhans cells in RHE model
evidence.experimental_conditions: Reconstructed human epidermal (RHE) model with incorporated CD34+ derived dendritic cells; topical application of DNCB.
evidence.support_text: Topical application of dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB) to a reconstructed human epidermal (RHE) model containing CD34+ derived dendritic cells induced CD86 expression on Langerhans cells (Facy et al., 2004).

evidence.assay_type: CD86 expression on Langerhans cells in RHE model
evidence.experimental_conditions: Reconstructed human epidermal (RHE) model with incorporated CD34+ derived dendritic cells; topical application of NiSO₄.
evidence.support_text: Topical application of NiSO₄ to a reconstructed human epidermal (RHE) model containing CD34+ derived dendritic cells induced CD86 expression on Langerhans cells (Facy et al., 2004).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rats consumed Cd in drinking water; concentration not specified; comparison of epidermis vs dermis.
evidence.support_text: Higher Cd concentration in epidermis compared to dermis was attributed to binding of Cd to SH groups of cysteine in epidermal keratins.

evidence.assay_type: electron microscopic observation of Langerhans cell morphology
evidence.experimental_conditions: DNCB application (0.25%) to guinea pig skin; examination at time points up to 96 h; electron microscopy
evidence.support_text: The LCs of both guinea pig strains showed similar cellular and endocytotic activation after DNCB application: enlargement of the cell and nucleus, numerous cytoplasmic organelles, and an increased number of endocytotic formations such as coated vesicles, coated pits, and Birbeck granules.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Epicutaneous sensitization, both Rockefeller strains (responder and non-responder), evaluation by electron microscopy
evidence.support_text: Epicutaneous sensitization with contact sensitizers, including DNCB, resulted in cellular and endocytotic activation of epidermal Langerhans cells, as observed by electron microscopy. evidence.experimental_conditions: 5 µg/mL imiquimod, 4 h exposure; human epidermal Langerhans cells (LC) purified by density gradient centrifugation and MACS (purity 84.48%); culture supernatants analyzed by ELISA
evidence.support_text: LC were cultured with 5 µg/mL imiquimod for 4 hours; IL-1β secreted from treated LC was higher than from control LC (p<0.05), measured by ELISA.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5 µg/mL imiquimod, 4 h exposure; human epidermal Langerhans cells (LC) purified by density gradient centrifugation and MACS (purity 84.48%); culture supernatants analyzed by ELISA

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5 µg/mL imiquimod, 4 h exposure; human epidermal Langerhans cells (LC) purified by density gradient centrifugation and MACS (purity 84.48%); culture supernatants analyzed by ELISA

evidence.support_text: Facy et al. used human CD34+-derived Langerhans cells incorporated into the EPISKIN construct, with detection of IL-1β up-regulation and CD86 expression as endpoints. The effects of benzocaine were also detected in this organotypic skin model system.

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo human skin organo-culture Langerhans cell migration assay

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo human skin organo-culture Langerhans cell migration assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: 24-hour exposure, diluted in water; tested at 300 and 500 ppm
evidence.support_text: Benzothiazolinone (BIT) showed a different Langerhans cell migration pattern compared to OIT after 24-hour exposure, and only OIT was able to induce migration to the basal lamina, implying that BIT did not induce this key event in the skin sensitization AOP.

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo human skin organo-culture Langerhans cell migration assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: 24-hour exposure, diluted in water; tested at 300 and 600 ppm
evidence.support_text: In an ex vivo human skin organo-culture model, octylisothiazolinone (OIT) induced Langerhans cell migration to the basal lamina of the epidermis after 24-hour exposure, as described for sensitizers. evidence.assay_type: ex vivo human skin sensitization organo-culture model (SSM) with DAB-stained Langerhans cell migration analysis
evidence.experimental_conditions: 24 h occlusive exposure, ex vivo human skin, water vehicle, high concentration
evidence.support_text: MI and BIT showed a Langerhans cells irritant distribution.

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo human skin sensitization organo-culture model (SSM) with DAB-stained Langerhans cell migration analysis
evidence.experimental_conditions: 24 h occlusive exposure, ex vivo human skin, water vehicle, high concentration
evidence.support_text: OIT-exposed skin presented a pattern where Langerhans cells were mostly located on the basal lamina as described in the literature for skin sensitizers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: applied to mouse skin in vivo
evidence.support_text: When DNCB was applied to mouse skin, Langerhans cells reduced their cell surface thiols, as detected by flow cytometry.

evidence.experimental_conditions: epicutaneous application on mouse skin; in vivo analysis of Langerhans cells
evidence.support_text: Epicutaneous application of 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB) on mouse skin significantly decreased cell surface thiols of Langerhans cells in vivo, as shown by flow cytometry.

evidence.assay_type: flow cytometry cell surface thiol measurement
evidence.experimental_conditions: epicutaneous application of 100 µl of 0.5% DNCB on shaved abdomens of BALB/c mice for 2 hours; epidermal cell suspensions stained with PE-conjugated anti-CD86 and Alexa Fluor 488 C5 maleimide; flow cytometry
evidence.support_text: Epidermal Langerhans cells decrease cell surface thiols after epicutaneous application of DNCB. Freshly shaved abdomens of BALB/c mice were painted with 100 µl of 0.5% DNCB. After 2 hours, epidermal cell suspensions were prepared and stained with PE-conjugated anti-CD86 antibody and Alexa Fluor 488 C5 maleimide. Cell surface thiols of CD86+ epidermal cells were compared between DNCB-treated and vehicle-treated mice. The mean ± SEM of relative fluorescence intensity (RFI) is shown, and asterisk indicates significant difference (P<0.05).

evidence.assay_type: Flow cytometry with thiol-reactive probe (mouse epidermal LC)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse ear skin, epicutaneous application of DNCB, 2 h
evidence.support_text: At 2 hours after DNCB painting, epidermal CD86+ Langerhans cells decreased their cell surface thiols.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Auricle tissue, HE staining, 24 h after final treatment (day 20).
evidence.support_text: Investigations also revealed that in all DNFB-treated mice, HE-stained auricle specimens showed signs of an allergic inflammatory response. Notably, the epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous tissue were thickened, and edema, hyperemia, and infiltration of inflammatory cells were observed in the thickened tissue samples. In addition, microabscesses were observed in the epidermis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Auricle tissue, HE staining, 24 h after final treatment.
evidence.support_text: In the auricular tissue of all TNCB-treated mice, the epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous tissue were thickened, with characteristic edema, hyperemia, and inflammatory cell infiltration being observed in the thickened tissue. Nevertheless, there were no microabscesses as observed in DNFB.

evidence.assay_type: histochemical uptake assay in viable human epidermis
evidence.experimental_conditions: applied CrCl₃ solution to viable human epidermis, histochemical detection
evidence.support_text: In an investigation studying the clearance mechanism for known, common contact sensitizers that enter the intercellular spaces of the epidermis, it was demonstrated histochemically, in viable human epidermis, that trivalent chromium (from an applied CrCl₃ solution) is selectively taken up by Langerhans cells.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Auricle tissue, staining not specified, observed 24 h after second application.
evidence.support_text: We observed that although the auricles of all DNFB-treated mice showed varied thickening of the epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous tissue, accompanied by edema and hyperemia in the thickened tissue, these reactions were not observed in the back skin.

evidence.assay_type: human Langerhans cell migration assay (anti-CD1a staining)
evidence.experimental_conditions: human volunteers, challenge with DNTB, biopsy after 18 h, removal of epidermis, anti-CD1a antibody staining
evidence.support_text: DNTB fails to induce Langerhans cell migration in human volunteers. Volunteers were challenged with DNTB or diluent control, biopsied after 18 h, and epidermal LCs were counted after anti-CD1a staining. The bar indicates mean migration for each group; DNTB did not induce migration.

evidence.assay_type: human skin explant LC migration assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: human skin explant cultures; all dose levels tested; marker: CD1a
evidence.support_text: At all dose levels tested, the monomethacrylate MMA showed the lowest migration indices in the human skin explant Langerhans cell migration assay, in line with clinical and experimental experiences (i.e., positive but weak).

evidence.assay_type: human skin explant LC migration assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: human skin explant cultures; dose: 10%; marker: CD1a
evidence.support_text: When tested at the lowest dose level (10%), the dimethacrylate EGDMA might be rated as the strongest sensitizer based on Langerhans cell migration index in human skin explants.

evidence.assay_type: human skin explant LC migration assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: human skin explant cultures; dose: 2% (undiluted? the text says 'already at 2%'); marker: CD1a
evidence.support_text: DNCB, known as a very strong sensitizer, showed a high migration index already at 2% in the human skin explant Langerhans cell migration assay using CD1a as marker.

evidence.assay_type: human skin explant LC migration assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: human skin explant cultures; dose: undiluted fluid; marker: CD1a
evidence.support_text: Testing allergens as undiluted fluids led to the highest migration indices for the mono-methacrylate HEMA in the human skin explant Langerhans cell migration assay.
In a murine LLNA, read-across material vanillyl butyl ether was found to be sensitizing with an EC3 value of 14.58% (3645 µg/cm²).
